chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
The day of the oppressed over the oppressor is severer than the day of the oppressor over the oppressed.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the Day of the Oppressed and the Day of the Oppressor?
ai.summary: In this profound saying from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates the asymmetry of divine justice, where the oppressor bears the weight of their own sins plus the accumulated rights of the oppressed, while the oppressed receives their due without deduction. This concept, central to Shia jurisprudence regarding *Haqq al-Nas* (rights of people), underscores that the oppressor's accountability is compounded by the victim's potential patience or immediate claim, making their reckoning more severe. It serves as a spiritual warning that temporary dominance does not equate to ultimate victory in the Hereafter.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 241. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
The day of the oppressed over the oppressor will be severer than the day of the oppressor over the oppressed. [1]
